units.explain: Coerces a config value into a timedelta. Returns None or an existing timedelta unchanged; any other value (per the declared type, an int) is interpreted as a number of seconds and wrapped via timedelta(seconds=value). Pure, no side effects, raises whatever timedelta raises for non-numeric input.
units.summary: Convert None/int values to timedelta, interpreting ints as seconds.

relations.basis: used as get_converter for the permanent_session_lifetime ConfigAttribute

units.explain: Framework-neutral core of the Flask application object, subclassing Scaffold. Acts as a central registry for URL rules, view functions, blueprints, error handlers, template configuration, JSON handling, and logging, while delegating WSGI dispatch to the concrete subclass in flask/app.py (not in this file). Class attributes are extension points: aborter_class, jinja_environment, app_ctx_globals_class, config_class, url_rule_class, url_map_class, json_provider_class, and test_client/test_cli_runner class hooks. ConfigAttribute descriptors (testing, secret_key, permanent_session_lifetime) proxy onto the config mapping; permanent_session_lifetime applies _make_timedelta as get_converter. jinja_options is a plain dict consumed only when the Jinja environment is first created. The later region (s0 continuation, lines 927-940) declares should_ignore_error = None, a deprecated placeholder documented as formerly deciding whether errors are skipped by teardown handlers. Instance state is initialized in __init__. Behavior after the first request is frozen for setup methods (see _check_setup_finished).
units.summary: Sans-IO Flask application core: registries, configuration attributes, and class-level extension hooks.
uncertainties: The concrete subclass in flask/app.py supplies WSGI __call__/dispatch; its behavior is outside this batch.
Whether should_ignore_error is still consulted anywhere is not provable from this source.

extras.note: testing, secret_key, and permanent_session_lifetime are ConfigAttribute proxies reading TESTING, SECRET_KEY, and PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME from app.config.

units.explain: Initializes the application. Delegates resource-path resolution (import_name, static_folder/static_url_path, template_folder, root_path) to Scaffold.__init__ first. Resolves the instance path: if not supplied it calls auto_find_instance_path(); if supplied it must be an absolute path or ValueError is raised. Then, in order: stores instance_path; builds config via make_config(instance_relative_config); creates aborter via make_aborter(); instantiates the JSON provider (json_provider_class(self)); initializes empty registries url_build_error_handlers, teardown_appcontext_funcs, shell_context_processors, blueprints (an ordered dict), and extensions; creates url_map via url_map_class(host_matching=host_matching); stores subdomain_matching; and sets _got_first_request = False as the setup-lock flag. No early returns; exceptions propagate from Scaffold.__init__, path resolution, or construction of config/aborter/url_map.
units.summary: Constructs app state: instance path, config, aborter, JSON provider, and empty registries.

extras.note: A relative instance_path raises ValueError with a message stating the path must be absolute.
_got_first_request is the latch consulted by _check_setup_finished to block late setup calls.

units.explain: Setup-lock guard. Raises AssertionError naming the forbidden method if _got_first_request is True; returns silently otherwise. Called by setup-decorated methods (via setupmethod in scaffold) to prevent registration changes after the app served its first request.
units.summary: Raises AssertionError if setup methods are called after the first request.

units.explain: Cached property returning the application display name. If import_name is '__main__', it reads the __main__ module's __file__; when absent returns the literal '__main__', otherwise returns the file's basename without extension. For any other import_name it returns import_name as-is. Result is cached on first access (werkzeug cached_property); a later assignment overrides the cache.
units.summary: Display name: basename of the run file when run as __main__, else import_name.
uncertainties: Exact caching semantics of werkzeug.utils.cached_property (including assignment override) are external behavior.

units.explain: Cached property returning the app's logging.Logger by delegating to flask.logging.create_logger(self). Per the docstring: the logger is named after the app, its level is set to DEBUG only during creation in debug mode, and a default handler is added only if no handlers are configured. Creation and handler wiring are external to this file; this unit only establishes the delegation and single-creation (cached) semantics.
units.summary: Lazily creates and caches the app logger via create_logger.

units.explain: Cached property that creates the Jinja environment on first access by calling create_jinja_environment(); subsequent accesses reuse the cached instance. Because creation is lazy and one-shot, mutating jinja_options after the first access has no effect. create_jinja_environment itself is abstract in this sansio base and raises NotImplementedError; the concrete implementation lives in flask/app.py, so any documented behavior of the produced Environment depends on that unproven boundary.
units.summary: Lazily builds and caches the Jinja environment on first access.
uncertainties: create_jinja_environment is not implemented in this file; environment construction details are outside this batch.

units.explain: Builds the config object. Chooses root_path or instance_path as the base directory depending on the instance_relative flag (passed from __init__'s instance_relative_config). Copies default_config into a plain dict, sets defaults['DEBUG'] from get_debug_flag() (environment-driven), and returns config_class(root_path, defaults) — by default flask.Config. Pure factory; no state stored here (the caller assigns it).
units.summary: Creates the Config object rooted at root or instance path with DEBUG default applied.

units.explain: Factory returning aborter_class() — by default werkzeug.exceptions.Aborter — assigned to app.aborter in __init__. The aborter is callable to raise HTTP errors; flask.abort delegates to it. No arguments, no state.
units.summary: Instantiates the Aborter used by flask.abort.

units.explain: Locates the instance directory when none was supplied. Calls find_package(self.import_name), which yields (prefix, package_path). If prefix is None (module resolved without an installed prefix) returns package_path/instance; otherwise returns prefix/var/<name>-instance, where name is the cached app name property. Filesystem-only computation; no directories are created here.
units.summary: Guesses the instance folder relative to the package or installs prefix.

relations.basis: uses self.name in the prefix branch

units.explain: Returns a DispatchingJinjaLoader(self) that dispatches template loading between the app's own loader and registered blueprints' loaders. Docstring discourages overriding this; subclasses should override jinja_loader instead. Any dispatch semantics live in flask/templating.py (external to this batch).
units.summary: Creates the dispatching Jinja loader covering app and blueprint templates.

units.explain: Decides Jinja autoescaping per template name. Returns True for None (unknown/inline names); otherwise True iff the case-insensitive (lowercased) filename ends with .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml, or .svg. Pure predicate.
units.summary: Enables autoescape for HTML/XML/SVG templates, always for unnamed ones.

units.explain: Getter/setter pair for debug mode. The getter reads config['DEBUG'] directly, so late changes to the config key are visible (docstring warns behavior may be surprising if set late). The setter writes config['DEBUG'] and, only when config['TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD'] is None (i.e., left at its automatic default), propagates the value to jinja_env.auto_reload; an explicit TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD value suppresses this side effect. Accessing jinja_env in the setter forces one-time environment creation if not yet built.
units.summary: Maps debug mode onto the DEBUG config key and syncs Jinja auto-reload.

extras.note: The setter touches jinja_env.auto_reload only when TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD is None, and this lazy-creates the Jinja environment.

units.explain: setupmethod-guarded registration of a Blueprint. Records nothing itself; it forwards directly to blueprint.register(self, options) after the setupmethod decorator enforces the pre-first-request constraint. Keyword options override blueprint defaults and flow into BlueprintSetupState (name option can re-register the same blueprint under an alias). Actual route/error-handler attachment and duplicate-name handling are the blueprint's register logic in flask/sansio/blueprints.py, an external boundary.
units.summary: Delegates blueprint registration to the blueprint's register method.
uncertainties: Duplicate-name collision behavior is decided inside Blueprint.register, not shown here.

units.explain: Returns self.blueprints.values(), a ValuesView iterating blueprints in registration order. Registration count is not tracked (re-registration under the same name keeps one entry).
units.summary: Iterates registered blueprints in registration order.

units.explain: Registers a URL rule. Resolution order: endpoint defaults to _endpoint_from_view_func(view_func) when omitted; methods come from options.pop('methods'), else view_func.methods, else ('GET',). A string passed as methods raises TypeError with guidance to pass a list. Methods are uppercased into a set. provide_automatic_options defaults from view_func.provide_automatic_options, else to OPTIONS-not-in-methods and config['PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS']; when truthy OPTIONS joins required_methods (taken from view_func.required_methods). required_methods are unioned into methods. A url_rule_class rule (default werkzeug Rule) is constructed with the merged methods and remaining options, its provide_automatic_options attribute set, and it is added to url_map. Finally, if view_func is given: an existing view_functions entry for the same endpoint with a different function raises AssertionError about overwriting an existing endpoint; identical re-registration is tolerated; otherwise the function is stored. setupmethod enforces the pre-first-request constraint. Note: registering the same rule with the same function re-adds the URL rule to the map.
units.summary: Validates and registers a URL rule and binds its view function to the endpoint.

relations.basis: @setupmethod decorator guards against calls after the first request

extras.note: Mapping a different view function under an existing endpoint raises AssertionError; re-registering the same function is allowed.
Passing methods as a plain string raises TypeError.

units.explain: Overloaded decorator family for registering Jinja filters. Usage forms: @app.template_filter (no parentheses), @app.template_filter('name'), or direct add_template_filter. If the first argument is callable (bare decorator form) the function is registered immediately under its own __name__ and returned; otherwise a decorator closure is returned that registers the function under the given name (or its __name__ when None) and returns it unchanged. Overload stubs exist purely for typing; the inner decorator functions are trivial returns. Registration mutates jinja_env.filters and is setupmethod-guarded, so calling after the first request is blocked. Touching jinja_env lazy-creates the environment; later jinja_options changes have no effect.
units.summary: Registers a function as a Jinja filter via decorator or direct call.

units.explain: Overloaded decorator family for registering Jinja tests, structurally identical to template_filter: bare-decorator form registers immediately under the function's __name__; parenthesized form returns a closure registering under the supplied name (or __name__ if None) and returns the function. Adds to jinja_env.tests via add_template_test; setupmethod-guarded; lazy-creates jinja_env.
units.summary: Registers a function as a Jinja test via decorator or direct call.

units.explain: Overloaded decorator family for registering Jinja globals, structurally identical to template_filter/template_test: bare-decorator form registers immediately under the function's __name__; parenthesized form returns a closure registering under the supplied name (or __name__ if None). Adds to jinja_env.globals via add_template_global; setupmethod-guarded; lazy-creates jinja_env.
units.summary: Registers a function as a Jinja global via decorator or direct call.

units.explain: setupmethod-guarded decorator that appends the function to teardown_appcontext_funcs and returns it unchanged. Per the docstring contract: functions run when the app context is popped (end of request, CLI command, or with-block exit); on an unhandled exception the function receives the error object, but if an errorhandler handled the exception teardown gets no error; return values are ignored; teardown functions must not raise. The actual invocation happens in context teardown code outside this file.
units.summary: Decorator registering a function to run at app-context teardown.
uncertainties: The exact pop/error-passing sequence lives in flask/ctx.py, not this batch.

units.explain: setupmethod-guarded decorator appending the function to shell_context_processors and returning it unchanged; processors supply variables when a flask shell context is created. Invocation happens in shell setup code outside this file.
units.summary: Decorator registering a shell context processor function.

units.explain: Locates an error handler for an exception. Normalizes the exception via _get_exc_class_and_code(type(e)) into (exc_class, code) — code being the HTTP status for HTTPException-like classes, else None. Builds a name list of the given blueprint names (outermost-to-innermost order supplied by the caller) followed by None for the app level. Iterates code levels: (code, None) when a code exists, else just (None); within each level iterates names, skips empty handler maps (error_handler_spec[name][c]), then walks exc_class.__mro__ returning the first non-None handler found in handler_map. Returns None if nothing matches. Net precedence: more specific code before generic, then blueprint before app, then nearest MRO ancestor.
units.summary: Finds a matching error handler by code, blueprint, and exception MRO order.
uncertainties: Blueprint-name ordering within the caller-supplied blueprints list is not established here.

units.explain: Decides whether an HTTP exception raised by a view should bypass error handlers and surface as a normal traceback. Returns True when config TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS is truthy. Otherwise consults TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS: when it is unset (None), debug mode is on, and the exception is a BadRequestKeyError, returns True (implicit-trap for key errors in debug); when set truthy, returns isinstance(e, BadRequest); otherwise returns False. Called by the concrete app's exception-handling pipeline (flask/app.py) — a True result means the registered handler for the exception is not invoked.
units.summary: Determines whether an HTTP exception should be re-raised instead of handled.

extras.note: TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS=None plus debug mode traps only BadRequestKeyError instances.

units.explain: Creates a redirect response by delegating to werkzeug's redirect with location, the given status code (default 303 since 3.2, formerly 302), and Response=self.response_class so the response type honors subclass customization. Called by flask.redirect; callable directly. Pure factory.
units.summary: Builds a redirect response using the app's response class.

units.explain: Overwrites below; see the correct unit id. This method injects URL defaults for an endpoint into the values dict before URL building. It starts with the app-level bucket (None) and, when the endpoint contains a dot, chains reversed(_split_blueprint_path(endpoint.rpartition('.')[0])[...]) so blueprint-level default functions run in leaf-to-root order. Parsing the endpoint from its dotted name (rather than reading request.blueprints) supports url_for outside a request context. For each name present in url_default_functions, every registered function is called with (endpoint, values), mutating values in place. No return value.
units.summary: Applies registered url_default_functions to values before URL building.

units.explain: Fallback handler invoked by url_for on werkzeug BuildError. Iterates url_build_error_handlers, calling each with (error, endpoint, values). A handler that raises BuildError has that exception adopted as the active error (loop continues with the new error); a handler returning None is skipped; any other return value is returned to url_for as the built URL. If all handlers are exhausted, the error is re-raised: bare `raise` when this call is running inside the original except block (error is sys.exc_info()[1]), otherwise explicit `raise error`. With no handlers registered this reduces to re-raising the BuildError.
units.summary: Runs url_build_error_handlers to recover from a BuildError or re-raise it.

extras.note: A registered handler raising BuildError replaces the current error and the loop continues; a handler returning None is skipped.

Overloaded decorator families (template_filter/test/global) grouped with their add_* helpers; property getter/setter pairs merged; class continuation region folded into the class unit.
